recipes.d: Soft gnocchi in a speedy tomato and spinach sauce
steps: Slice the onion finely and soften it in a little oil for 3 minutes.
Stir in the passata and simmer gently while the gnocchi cooks according to its packet instructions.
Fold in the spinach until wilted, then drain the gnocchi and stir it through the sauce.
Scatter over the mozzarella and heat until melted and piping hot before serving.

recipes.d: Quick pitta pizzas for an easy family supper
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and arrange the pittas on a tray.
Spread each pitta with passata and top with chopped peppers, sweetcorn and torn mozzarella.
Bake for 8–10 minutes until the cheese bubbles and the pittas are crisp at the edges.
Allow the pizzas to cool slightly, then serve with any extra vegetables.

recipes.d: Toasted bagels with warm tuna and cheddar
steps: Heat the grill, split the bagels and drain the tuna thoroughly.
Mix tuna, mayonnaise and sweetcorn, then spoon over the cut bagel halves.
Top with grated cheese and grill for 3–5 minutes until the cheese is bubbling.
Serve hot, checking the filling has heated through.

recipes.d: Warm pitta pockets with golden halloumi and crunchy peppers
steps: Slice the halloumi and peppers into strips and warm the pittas according to their packet instructions.
Fry the halloumi in a non-stick pan until golden on both sides.
Mix the yoghurt with a little water to make a spoonable dressing.
Fill the pittas with lettuce, pepper strips and halloumi, then drizzle with yoghurt.

recipes.d: One-pan butter beans in a creamy tomato sauce
steps: Finely chop the onion and soften it in a pan with a little oil.
Drain and rinse the butter beans, then add them with the passata and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the cream cheese and spinach until the sauce is smooth and the greens have wilted.
Check the beans are piping hot and serve with toasted bread.

recipes.d: Crisp toasted wraps filled with mushrooms and melting cheese
steps: Slice the mushrooms and cook in a hot pan until their moisture has evaporated.
Add spinach and stir briefly until wilted, then remove the vegetables from the heat.
Share the filling and grated cheese between the wraps, folding each into a parcel.
Toast each parcel in a dry pan on both sides until golden and the cheese is fully melted.

recipes.d: Cool, creamy wraps that need no cooking
steps: Wash the cucumber and lettuce, then slice them thinly.
Spread the wraps with cream cheese, leaving a small border at the edges.
Layer with smoked salmon, cucumber and lettuce.
Roll tightly, slice in half and serve immediately; refrigerate any leftovers promptly.

recipes.d: A filling one-pan chicken and gnocchi dinner
steps: Cut the chicken into small, even pieces and fry in a little oil until cooked all the way through.
Cook the gnocchi according to its packet instructions and reserve a little cooking water.
Add spinach to the chicken pan until wilted, then stir through the pesto and gnocchi.
Loosen with a splash of cooking water, scatter over cheese and serve piping hot.

recipes.d: Garlicky noodles with prawns, peppers and greens
steps: Cook the noodles according to their packet instructions and drain.
Slice the peppers and soften them in a frying pan with the garlic.
Add the cooked prawns and spinach; stir-fry until the prawns are piping hot and the spinach wilts.
Toss in the noodles and soy sauce, heat thoroughly and serve immediately.

recipes.d: Warm filled flatbreads for busy evenings
steps: Cut the chicken into small pieces and slice the peppers.
Fry the chicken until fully cooked, then add the peppers and cook until tender.
Stir in the passata and simmer for 4 minutes until the mixture is hot and thickened.
Warm the flatbreads and fill with the chicken mixture and fresh lettuce.

recipes.d: A simple family stir-fry with beef and broccoli
steps: Slice the beef thinly across the grain, chop the onion and cut the broccoli into small florets.
Cook the noodles as directed on the packet and steam the broccoli until just tender.
Stir-fry the beef and onion in a hot pan until the beef is fully cooked.
Add broccoli, noodles and soy sauce, toss until piping hot and serve.

recipes.d: Quick microwave potatoes with a hearty bean topping
steps: Prick the potatoes all over and microwave in batches until completely tender, following your microwave's guidance.
Drain and rinse the black beans, then warm them with the salsa in a saucepan until piping hot.
Split the cooked potatoes carefully and fluff the centres with a fork.
Spoon over the hot beans, scatter with cheddar and allow the cheese to melt.

recipes.d: Family-friendly pasta with ham, sweetcorn and a light dressing
steps: Cook the pasta according to the packet instructions until tender, then drain and cool promptly.
Cook the sweetcorn until hot and cool it before mixing into the salad.
Dice the ham and mix with the pasta, sweetcorn, yoghurt and grated cheese.
Serve freshly made or chill immediately in a covered container until needed.

recipes.d: Tender pork strips and peppers with thick noodles
steps: Slice the pork into thin strips, chop the onion and peppers, and prepare the udon as directed.
Fry the pork in a hot pan until thoroughly cooked.
Add the onion and peppers, cooking until tender.
Toss with the drained udon and soy sauce, heating until everything is piping hot.

recipes.n: Easy eggs in tomato & pepper sauce
recipes.d: An easy pan of poached eggs in spiced tomato sauce
steps: Chop the onion and peppers and soften them in a wide pan.
Add passata and simmer for 8–10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Make eight small hollows, crack an egg into each and cover the pan until the whites are fully set.
Serve immediately with toasted bread; cook yolks thoroughly for anyone who needs fully cooked eggs.

recipes.d: One-pot orzo with prawns and a rich tomato sauce
steps: Finely chop and soften the onion in a little oil.
Add the orzo, passata, stock and enough water to cover; simmer and stir until the orzo is tender.
Fold through the cooked prawns and spinach and cook until the prawns are piping hot.
Check the pasta is cooked and the sauce is not dry, then serve promptly.

recipes.d: A filling, inexpensive bean supper on toast
steps: Chop the onion finely and soften it in a pan for a few minutes.
Drain and rinse the beans, add with the passata and simmer until thoroughly hot.
Toast the bread and arrange it on serving plates.
Spoon beans onto the toast, top with grated cheese and let it melt before eating.

recipes.d: Microwave jacket potatoes topped with a warm tuna filling
steps: Prick the potatoes and microwave in batches until the centres are soft and fully cooked.
Drain the tuna and heat the sweetcorn until piping hot.
Mix tuna, warm sweetcorn and yoghurt in a saucepan, stirring gently until heated through.
Split the potatoes, add the filling and scatter cheddar over the top.

recipes.d: Golden sausage pieces with peppers and tomato in wraps
steps: Remove sausage meat from the casings if needed and divide into small pieces.
Fry the sausage pieces until browned and cooked all the way through.
Add sliced peppers and onion, then stir through the passata and cook until tender.
Warm the wraps and fill with the sausage and pepper mixture while hot.

recipes.d: Warm falafel, crisp salad and creamy yoghurt in flatbreads
steps: Heat the falafel according to the packet directions until piping hot.
Wash and slice the cucumber and lettuce.
Warm the flatbreads and spoon a little plain yoghurt over each.
Fill with hot falafel and crunchy salad, then serve.
